character_sheet: A hostile crystal urchin: seventeen spines on one pivot - a 30-tall central spine, four 25-long and four 20-long spines fanned upward around it, and eight 8-long spines splayed downward as feet (ModelUrchin.java:64-130) - drawn at x1.25. 25 HP, 10 damage, 4 armour, speed 0.3, fire-immune (Urchin.java:82-89; ModEntities.java:172-175). It sheds flame particles (:118-123) and burns in water, hurting itself and smoking (:124-135). On a 1-in-8 tick it picks the nearest living thing in a 16-block box - not the Crystal dimension's other creatures nor a creative player (:164-184, :209-240) - walks at 1.2 and, within 2.8 blocks, raises its attacking flag and one time in seven bites for 10 and five seconds of fire (:105-109, :171-176). It spawns in the dark in the night half of the day with six air blocks around its head (:268-284) and despawns in daylight unless a Crystal Urchin spawner made it (:138-147). Read it as a spiky crystal star: the feet scuttling, the crown of spines slowly turning and swaying, a fast spin when it is about to bite.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.25 of the rig (UrchinRenderer.java:25, :38; shadow 0.4375, :27) on a 128x128 sheet (ModelUrchin.java:132), urchin.png (UrchinRenderer.java:20); the hitbox is 1.35 x 2.1 (ModEntities.java:172-175). The original's ModelUrchin(1.0f) argument was the wingspeed (ModelUrchin.java:21), not a scale. Every part is a 1-wide spine on the same pivot at y 16.

groups.name: gait
groups.axis: x (the inner feet and of3 / of4) and z (of1 / of2)
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad (27 deg) x the walking speed above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 about each foot's splay rest (±0.261 inner, ±0.523 outer); the four outer feet share one rhythm at 0.7 rad/tick, the four inner feet run at 1.7, 1.65, 1.75 and 1.8 so they never line up; 0 below the threshold
groups.plain: the eight downward spines scuttle: the outer four rock together, the inner four paddle at four slightly different rates
groups.math: n = cos(t * 0.7) * pi * 0.15 * amount; n1..n4 = cos(t * 1.7 / 1.65 / 1.75 / 1.8) * pi * 0.15 * amount (all 0 when amount <= 0.1); if1.xRot = 0.261 + n1; if2.xRot = -0.261 - n2; if3.xRot = n3; if4.xRot = -n4; of1.zRot = -0.523 + n; of2.zRot = 0.523 - n; of3.xRot = -0.523 + n; of4.xRot = 0.523 - n
groups.phase: the limbSwingAmount threshold of 0.1 gates it
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.7 for the outer feet (an 8.98-tick period); the inner feet run at 1.7 / 1.65 / 1.75 / 1.8 (3.5-3.8 ticks)

groups.name: spin
groups.amplitude: a continuous turn: calm at 0.02 rad/tick (one turn every 314 ticks); attacking at 0.2 rad/tick (one turn every 31 ticks)
groups.plain: the central spine turns steadily about the vertical - a slow creep at rest, a fast spin while the attacking flag is up
groups.phase: the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (Urchin.java:45-46, set 1 within 2.8 blocks of a target on the 1-in-8 pass :171-173, 0 with no target :180-182) selects the rate
groups.omega_note: not a cosine: a linear spin wrapped at 2 pi - 314 ticks per turn calm, 31 attacking

groups.name: crown
groups.amplitude: calm: pi x 0.02 = 0.063 rad (3.6 deg) on eight rhythms at 0.07 / 0.065 / 0.075 / 0.08 / 0.055 / 0.045 / 0.035 / 0.04 rad/tick; attacking: pi x 0.06 = 0.188 rad (11 deg) on the same eight rhythms ten times faster (0.7 / 0.65 / 0.75 / 0.8 / 0.55 / 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.4); each of the eight spines takes one rhythm on x and another on z about its splay rest
groups.plain: the eight upward spines sway on two axes each at eight unrelated rates: a slow shimmer at rest, a fast shiver while attacking
groups.math: n1..n8 = cos(t * r_i) * pi * A with (r, A) = calm (0.07, 0.065, 0.075, 0.08, 0.055, 0.045, 0.035, 0.04; 0.02) or attacking (x10; 0.06); tis1.xRot = 0.261 + n1; tis2.xRot = -0.261 + n2; tis3.xRot = n3; tis4.xRot = n4; tis1.zRot = n5; tis2.zRot = n6; tis3.zRot = 0.261 + n7; tis4.zRot = -0.261 + n8; tos1.xRot = -0.532 + n1; tos2.xRot = n7; tos3.xRot = n3; tos4.xRot = 0.532 + n5; tos1.zRot = n4; tos2.zRot = -0.523 + n6; tos3.zRot = 0.523 + n2; tos4.zRot = n8
groups.phase: the synched DATA_ATTACKING int selects the rate and width
groups.omega_note: the classic phases are ageInTicks x 0.035-0.08 calm (79-180 ticks) and x 0.35-0.8 attacking (7.9-18 ticks)

behaviour: One gait rhythm above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 (ModelUrchin.java:146-166): the eight downward spines scuttle 27 degrees x the walking speed about their splay rests, the outer four together at 0.7 rad/tick and the inner four at 1.7, 1.65, 1.75 and 1.8 rad/tick, so the feet never fall into step.

Two branches on the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (Urchin.java:45-46), which the 1-in-8 pass sets to 1 within 2.8 blocks of a target (:171-173) and clears when it has none (:180-182): calm, the central spine creeps round once every 314 ticks and the eight upward spines shimmer 3.6 degrees on eight slow rhythms (0.035-0.08 rad/tick); attacking, the spine spins once every 31 ticks and the crown shivers 11 degrees at ten times the rate (:167-204). Note the flag stays 1 while the target is merely out of reach (:177-179 sets nothing), so the fast spin also plays during the chase.

There is no head and no look: every part sits on one pivot at y 16. The bite (doHurtTarget, Urchin.java:105-109: 10 and five seconds of fire, one time in seven on the pass) and the water burn (:133-135) draw no pose.

formulas: `ModelUrchin.poseFrom` (ModelUrchin.java:144-213; orig ModelUrchin.java:155-212 in `render` (func_78088_a, :141-230; func_78087_a at :238-240 is a bare super call), wingspeed 1.0 from `new ModelUrchin(1.0f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:487 - the port's WINGSPEED): while the walking speed is above a tenth five swings are the cosines of the age in ticks times 0.7, 1.7, 1.65, 1.75 and 1.8 times the wingspeed, each times pi, times 0.15, times the walking speed, else 0: the four inner fins pitch 0.261 plus the second, -0.261 minus the third, the fourth, and minus the fifth; the first two outer fins roll -0.523 plus the first swing and 0.523 minus it, the last two pitch the same. Attacking, the centre yaws by the age times 0.2 modulo two pi and the eight spine rocks are the cosines of the age times 0.7, 0.65, 0.75, 0.8, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35 and 0.4 times the wingspeed, each times pi, times 0.06; not attacking, the centre yaws by the age times 0.02 modulo two pi and the rocks are the cosines of the age times 0.07, 0.065, 0.075, 0.08, 0.055, 0.045, 0.035 and 0.04 times the wingspeed, each times pi, times 0.02. The four inner spines pitch 0.261 plus the first rock, -0.261 plus the second, the third, and the fourth, and roll the fifth, the sixth, 0.261 plus the seventh and -0.261 plus the eighth; the four outer spines pitch -0.532 plus the first, the seventh, the third and 0.532 plus the fifth, and roll the fourth, -0.523 plus the sixth, 0.523 plus the second and the eighth. The walk position and the head angles play no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (UrchinGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
